bindings.claim: Gateway routes POST /links to the link service, which dedupes on a client Idempotency-Key and the unique alias constraint before inserting the immutable mapping into Links DB, then write-through populates Redis so the first redirect is already a cache hit.

GET /{code} resolves via Redis (write-through on create); miss reads the replica, and replica miss/outage escalates to the primary, closing the replication-lag false-miss. A click event is durably appended to a local outbox before the 302 returns, then relayed to the queue with retry-until-ack.

Dashboard query goes through gateway/service to the decoupled Counts Store, refreshed from the durable outbox→queue(16 partitions)→aggregator(16 consumers) every 30s — inside the 5-min bound, with idempotent upserts and monitored lag/backlog alerts.

Hop budget: hit path gateway5+service10+cache5+outbox-append2=22ms. Cache-miss-to-replica adds the failed 5ms lookup: 5+10+5+15+2=37ms. Worst-case replica-miss escalation to primary adds 10ms more: 47ms. All under the 50ms p99 budget.

Fallback now chains cache→replica→primary, so neither alone is a dead-end SPOF; a promoted replica assumes the primary's logical identity, and a fresh standby auto-reprovisions within minutes, restoring two-tier redundancy before a second failure in the same month.

Click events are durably outboxed before the redirect returns, relayed at-least-once to a 16-partition queue, and aggregated every 30s by 16 parallel consumers with idempotent dedup — well under 5 minutes, with monitoring alerting on backlog/lag before the bound is breached.
Links DB is a single Postgres instance indexed on short code; 20 million rows is well within one instance's capacity with headroom before sharding would ever be needed.

At 2,000 rps average, most reads hit the write-through cache; residual misses go to the replica, and any replica miss/outage escalates to the primary — so steady load never dead-ends on a single component, and no write contends with redirects.

At 10,000 rps peak the cache serves most reads; the peak-sized replica and primary escalation cover misses. Click durability runs via outbox→16-partition queue→16 aggregator consumers (16,000 events/sec capacity) — no write contends with redirects.

narrative.overview: The panel's fixes center on three real gaps. The hot-standby replica was a dead end: a replica miss (replication lag on a just-created link) or outage had no further fallback, and one promotion used up the month's redundancy. I added a direct replica-miss escalation to the primary — always current, since creates land there first — closing the false-miss window and removing the replica as a sole dependency; a promoted replica also assumes the primary's logical identity, and a fresh standby auto-reprovisions within minutes. Second, the click emit was truly fire-and-forget, silently dropping events on a failed enqueue. I added a durable local outbox: the service appends to it (~2ms) before the redirect returns, and a relay drains it into the queue with retry-until-ack. Third, the queue fed one aggregator with no stated parallelism against a 10k/s peak; it now has 16 partitions and 16 parallel consumers (16,000 events/sec capacity), plus backlog/lag thresholds on monitoring so a stall is caught before the 5-minute bound. I also corrected the latency sum — the miss path was missing the failed cache lookup's own 5ms — and added outbox and worst-case primary-escalation hops: 22/37/47ms, all under 50ms. Create now honors a client idempotency key and the alias-uniqueness constraint so a retry can't duplicate a link.

componentRationales.prose: The marketer and the visitor are the same client surface: one issues creates and reads the dashboard, the other just follows redirects. No change requested here.

Still a thin router with a declared 5ms hop budget and metrics emission. createLink now carries idempotent:true with a note that it forwards a client Idempotency-Key and relies on the service's dedupe plus the unique alias constraint — the gateway itself does no dedup logic, it just passes the header through.

Still the sole owner of create and redirect logic, now with seven distinct operations: cacheRead/cachePopulate, dbWriteCreate (idempotent, alias-unique, 409 on collision), dbReadFallback to the replica, a new dbReadFallbackPrimary that escalates past a replica miss or outage to the always-current primary, appendClickEvent (durably writes to the local outbox before replying), and readClickCounts. No operation does double duty, and the redirect path no longer dead-ends on one fallback tier.

Unchanged: write-through on create via cachePopulate (e-3), no TTL needed since mappings are immutable. A miss here is no longer a last resort — it escalates through the replica and, if needed, the primary, so this cache being cold never means a failed redirect.

Still the single system of record for the immutable mapping and now explicitly the fallback-of-last-resort when the replica misses or is down — it's always current because creates write here first. Its config now states it's a logical role: a promoted replica assumes this identity via DNS/VIP cutover, so create-after-failover needs no new edge.

Sized for 100% of peak and promotable, but the panel was right that a bare replica swap doesn't close an availability SPOF — it just moves it. It now escalates its own misses to the primary instead of dead-ending, and a new config value states the re-provisioning story the panel asked for: a fresh standby auto-provisions from the newly promoted primary within minutes, so the design tolerates more than one failure a month, not just one.
Durable, at-least-once log, now explicitly partitioned (16) so a single consumer can't become the peak-time bottleneck the panel flagged — sized with headroom over the 10,000/sec peak.

Batches every 30 seconds with idempotent, keyed upserts, now with 16 parallel consumer instances at ~1,000 events/sec each — 16,000/sec capacity against a 10,000/sec peak, so the single-consumer fan-in risk the panel named is closed with a stated number, not an assumption.
Unchanged: the counter lives here, decoupled from the immutable link row.

Now also watches queue backlog and aggregator lag, not just p99 latency and availability — new edges from the queue, the aggregator, and the outbox feed it metrics, so a stalled consumer or a backed-up relay breaches the 5-minute bound loudly, before a marketer notices a stale count.

New: the panel correctly called out that firing a click event straight into a queue with no ack or retry silently drops it on any blip. The service now appends the event here durably (~2ms) before the redirect returns; a relay drains it into the queue with retry-until-ack, so delivery survives a broker outage without blocking the redirect on the broker itself.

criterionNarrations.prose: Create still goes gateway→service→one immutable insert, but now the gateway forwards a client Idempotency-Key the service dedupes against, and the unique alias constraint turns a collision into an explicit 409 instead of silent duplication — the retry-duplicate gap the panel found is closed without changing the create shape.

Redirect reads cache, then the replica, then — new — the primary if the replica itself misses or is down, so a just-created link within the replication-lag window still resolves instead of false-missing, and the replica is no longer the lone dependency standing between a redirect and a 404. The click event is durably outboxed before the 302 returns.

The dashboard count is built off a durable outbox, a 16-partition queue, and a 16-consumer aggregator, with monitoring now watching backlog and lag directly — freshness and correctness are both backed by stated numbers, not just the 30-second interval.

Corrected hop sums: hit path 5+10+5+2(outbox)=22ms; cache-and-replica miss adds the failed 5ms lookup plus the 15ms replica hop = 37ms; the worst case, replica-miss escalating to the primary, adds 10ms more = 47ms. All three stay under the 50ms p99 budget, with the audit trail now including every hop the panel said was missing.

Availability no longer rests on one hot standby alone: a replica miss or outage escalates to the primary instead of failing, so neither tier is a dead end on its own. A promoted replica assumes the primary's logical identity, and a fresh standby auto-reprovisions within minutes, so the 99.95% target isn't spent after a single failure in the month.

Click events are durably outboxed, relayed at-least-once through a 16-partition queue, and aggregated every 30 seconds by 16 parallel consumers with idempotent dedup — staleness stays far under 5 minutes, and monitoring now alerts on backlog or lag before the bound would ever be breached.

20 million indexed rows is a non-issue for a single Postgres primary; this was never actually threatened by the availability or durability fixes, which concern failover and event delivery, not row volume.

At steady 2,000 rps the cache absorbs nearly all traffic, the replica covers the rest, and a replica miss now escalates to the primary instead of dead-ending — average load stays decoupled from write risk and from the single-tier fallback gap the panel flagged.

At peak 10,000 rps the same cache-plus-replica-plus-primary chain holds for redirects, and the click pipeline — outbox→16-partition queue→16 aggregator consumers, 16,000 events/sec capacity — now has a stated number backing it instead of an assumed single consumer.

Links are inserted once via dbWriteCreate and never updated; the only new write-side behavior is the alias-uniqueness check that turns a collision into a 409 rather than an overwrite, so immutability still holds with no update operation anywhere in the graph.
